intro: Welcome back, detective! You can already guess about now with must be, might be and can't be. Today you go back in time: the floor is wet, so it must have rained. You'll also learn a subtle pair, needn't have and didn't need to, for things that weren't necessary.
teachingNotes: Recap in one line, don't re-teach: from b1-modals-deduction-present the learner knows must be (pasti), might / may / could be (mungkin), might not be (mungkin tidak) and can't / couldn't be (tidak mungkin) for guesses about NOW. New today: the same scale for the PAST = modal + have + past participle (bentuk ketiga / V3, known from the present perfect): must have gone, might have forgotten, can't have seen. Contrast now vs past: 'He must be at home' (now) vs 'He must have gone home' (earlier); 'You must be tired' vs 'You must have been tired'. Also contrast must have (pasti sudah, a guess) with had to (harus, a past obligation): 'He had to go home' vs 'He must have gone home'.

Common errors and why: *'He must went home already' -> 'He must have gone home already' (Indonesian has no tense, so learners put the past on the modal or the verb; in English the past is shown by have + V3). *'She can't has seen it' -> 'She can't have seen it' (have never changes after a modal: no has, no had). *'He must have went' -> 'must have gone' (third form, not the past form). *'You must have tired' -> 'You must have been tired' (be is not dropped). *'He mustn't have known' -> 'He can't have known' (mustn't = dilarang; Americans sometimes say 'must not have', accept it as American but teach can't have). *'must of' is a spelling mistake: must've sounds like 'must of', but it's have.

Choosing the degree: evidence NOW points back to a cause EARLIER (the floor is wet -> it must have rained). Strong evidence or only one sensible explanation -> must have; one clue or many possible reasons -> might / may / could have; the evidence makes it impossible -> can't / couldn't have; a known fact -> past simple (did / didn't). Only test clear cases. might, may and could have are all correct for 'not sure' (never mark may / could wrong where might fits); couldn't have = can't have. 'could have' also has another job ('You could have called me!' = kamu kan bisa menelepon): mention only, don't test it. mungkin tidak = might not have, tidak mungkin = can't have.

needn't have + V3 vs didn't need to + base verb: needn't have done = you DID it, but it turned out unnecessary (ternyata tidak perlu, padahal sudah): 'I needn't have brought an umbrella' (I brought it). didn't need to do = it wasn't necessary, and usually you didn't do it (tidak perlu, jadi tidak): 'I didn't need to bring an umbrella' (usually I didn't). didn't need to = didn't have to (known from B1). Be honest that didn't need to doesn't always say whether it happened ('I didn't need to bring it, but I did'); only needn't have clearly says it happened. Test only clear cases where the story says whether the action happened. Errors: *'needn't have bring' -> 'needn't have brought'; *'didn't need to brought' -> 'didn't need to bring'; *'needn't to have'. needn't have is more British and a bit formal; Americans more often say 'didn't need to / didn't have to … after all'.

Limits: should have / shouldn't have only as a note (seharusnya, regret or criticism: taught in b2-wish-regrets); needn't have = unnecessary, wasted effort, not wrong. No third conditional, no wish / if only, no will have for deduction ('He'll have left by now'), no passive modal perfects (must have been stolen): if a learner meets one, call it a phrase to remember. must have been + -ing (She must have been sleeping = pasti sedang tidur tadi) may be shown, not tested. B2 contexts: offices and meetings in Jakarta, KRL / MRT, Grab and ojek online, airports, campuses, kos life, rupiah.

keyPoints.title: must have, might have, can't have + the third form
keyPoints.explanation: For a guess about the past, use must / might / may / could / can't / couldn't + have + the third form (past participle: gone, seen, eaten). have never changes (no has, no had) and the verb is always the third form: not 'must went', not 'can't has seen', not 'must have went'. With be: must have been + adjective (You must have been tired).

examples.en: Budi's desk is empty and his bag is gone. He must have gone home.
examples.id: Meja Budi kosong dan tasnya tidak ada. Dia pasti sudah pulang.

examples.en: Sari isn't here yet. She might have overslept.
examples.id: Sari belum datang. Dia mungkin kesiangan.

examples.en: They can't have seen us. They were looking the other way.
examples.id: Mereka tidak mungkin melihat kita. Mereka sedang melihat ke arah lain.

id.title: must have, might have, can't have + bentuk ketiga
id.explanation: Untuk dugaan tentang masa lalu, pakai must / might / may / could / can't / couldn't + have + bentuk ketiga (past participle / V3: gone, seen, eaten). have tidak pernah berubah (bukan has, bukan had) dan kata kerjanya selalu bentuk ketiga: bukan 'must went', bukan 'can't has seen', bukan 'must have went'. Dengan be: must have been + kata sifat (You must have been tired).

keyPoints.title: needn't have done vs didn't need to do
keyPoints.explanation: needn't have + third form = you DID it, but later it turned out it wasn't necessary (ternyata tidak perlu, padahal sudah). didn't need to + base verb = it wasn't necessary, and usually you didn't do it (tidak perlu, jadi tidak). The question to ask: did it happen?

examples.en: I needn't have brought an umbrella. It didn't rain all day.
examples.id: Ternyata aku tidak perlu bawa payung (padahal sudah bawa). Seharian tidak hujan.

examples.en: I didn't need to bring an umbrella. The event was indoors.
examples.id: Aku tidak perlu bawa payung (jadi tidak bawa). Acaranya di dalam ruangan.

id.title: needn't have done vs didn't need to do
id.explanation: needn't have + bentuk ketiga = kamu SUDAH melakukannya, tapi ternyata tidak perlu (padahal sudah). didn't need to + kata kerja dasar = tidak perlu, dan biasanya kamu tidak melakukannya (tidak perlu, jadi tidak). Pertanyaan kuncinya: apakah itu terjadi?

keyPoints.title: From evidence now to what happened: the past scale
keyPoints.explanation: Look at the evidence you have now, then guess what happened before. From most sure (yes) to most sure (no): did (a fact) → must have done (almost sure: yes) → might / may / could have done (not sure) → might not / may not have done (not sure, maybe not) → can't / couldn't have done (almost sure: no) → didn't do (a fact). Not mustn't have: for 'tidak mungkin' use can't have.

examples.en: The floor is wet. It must have rained.
Rina might not have read my email. She's on leave this week.
examples.id: Rina mungkin belum membaca emailku. Minggu ini dia cuti.

examples.en: Dimas can't have cooked this. He doesn't know how to cook.
examples.id: Dimas tidak mungkin memasak ini. Dia tidak bisa masak.

id.title: Dari bukti sekarang ke apa yang terjadi: skala masa lalu
id.explanation: Lihat bukti yang kamu punya sekarang, lalu duga apa yang terjadi sebelumnya. Dari paling yakin (ya) sampai paling yakin (tidak): did (fakta) → must have done (hampir pasti ya) → might / may / could have done (tidak yakin) → might not / may not have done (tidak yakin, mungkin tidak) → can't / couldn't have done (hampir pasti tidak) → didn't do (fakta). Bukan mustn't have: untuk 'tidak mungkin' pakai can't have.

assessment.prompt: Correct the mistake: Budi can't has finished the report already. He only started it ten minutes ago.
acceptableAnswers: budi can't have finished the report already
budi cannot have finished the report already
budi couldn't have finished the report already
budi can't have already finished the report
he can't have finished the report already
budi can't have finished the report already he only started it ten minutes ago
budi cannot have finished the report already he only started it ten minutes ago
budi couldn't have finished the report already he only started it ten minutes ago
assessment.rubric: Correct: Budi can't / cannot / couldn't have finished the report already (after a modal, have never changes: no has). 'can't have finish' or 'can't have finished' with another small slip = 50. 'mustn't have finished' = 30 (mustn't = dilarang). 'might not have finished' = 40 (the evidence is strong). Keeping 'can't has' = 0.

assessment.prompt: Before the meeting, you left a full glass of iced coffee on your desk. Now it's empty, and there's a straw in it that isn't yours. Complete with the right form of drink: Somebody must ___ my coffee.
acceptableAnswers: have drunk
must have drunk
must've drunk
somebody must have drunk my coffee
somebody must've drunk my coffee
assessment.rubric: Correct: have drunk (must + have + the third form: drink, drank, drunk). 'have drank' = 50 (drank is the past form; the third form is drunk). 'has drunk' = 40 (have never changes after a modal). 'drank' alone (must drank) = 20.

assessment.prompt: Budi failed his driving test three times. Yesterday he proudly showed you his new driving licence (SIM). Complete with must have, might have or can't have and the verb pass: He ___ the test this time.
acceptableAnswers: must have passed
must've passed
he must have passed the test this time
he must've passed the test this time
assessment.rubric: Correct: must have passed (the new licence is strong evidence: only one sensible explanation). 'might have passed' = 40 (possible English, but the evidence is strong). 'must have pass' = 50 (third form needed). 'must passed' = 30. 'can't have passed' = 0 (the evidence says the opposite).

assessment.prompt: Rina says she saw Pak Hasan at the Bandung office yesterday afternoon. But you were with Pak Hasan at a conference in Surabaya all day yesterday. Complete with must have, might have or can't have: He ___ been in Bandung yesterday afternoon.
acceptableAnswers: can't have
cannot have
couldn't have
could not have
he can't have been in bandung yesterday afternoon
he cannot have been in bandung yesterday afternoon
he couldn't have been in bandung yesterday afternoon
assessment.rubric: Correct: can't / cannot / couldn't have (you were with him in Surabaya, so it's impossible). 'mustn't have' = 30 (mustn't = dilarang; American 'must not have' = 60). 'might not have' = 40 (the evidence is strong, not 'not sure'). 'must have' or 'might have' = 0.

assessment.prompt: Sari is 20 minutes late for the morning meeting. She isn't answering her phone, and you have no idea why: there are many possible reasons. Write one guess with might have, using: she / miss / the bus.
acceptableAnswers: she might have missed the bus
sari might have missed the bus
she might've missed the bus
sari might've missed the bus
assessment.rubric: Correct: She might have missed the bus. 'may have' or 'could have missed' = 90 (same meaning, but the item asks for might). 'might have miss' or 'might missed' = 50. 'must have missed' = 30 (you have no idea, so you can't be almost sure). 'might be missed' = 20.

assessment.prompt: You cooked a big pot of rendang for your guests. When they arrived, they told you they had already eaten at a restaurant. Complete with cook so that the sentence shows you DID cook, but it wasn't necessary: I ___ so much food.
acceptableAnswers: needn't have cooked
need not have cooked
i needn't have cooked so much food
i need not have cooked so much food
assessment.rubric: Correct: needn't / need not have cooked (you cooked, and it turned out unnecessary: ternyata tidak perlu, padahal sudah). 'didn't need to cook' = 50 (correct English, but it doesn't show that you cooked). 'needn't have cook' = 50 (third form needed). 'shouldn't have cooked' = 30 (that means it was a mistake, not just unnecessary).

assessment.prompt: Rina planned to book a Grab to Gambir station. Then her brother offered to drive her there, so she didn't book one. Complete with needn't have or didn't need to and the verb book: She ___ a Grab.
acceptableAnswers: didn't need to book
did not need to book
she didn't need to book a grab
she did not need to book a grab
assessment.rubric: Correct: didn't need to book (it wasn't necessary, and she didn't book one: tidak perlu, jadi tidak). 'didn't have to book' = 90 (same meaning, but the item asks for one of the two forms). 'didn't need to booked' = 50. 'needn't have booked' = 20 (that says she DID book one).

material.title: must have, might have, can't have + the third form

blocks.text:
**Quick recap:** about **now**, you already say *He **must be** at home* (pasti), *He **might be** at home* (mungkin) and *He **can't be** at home* (tidak mungkin).

Today the guess is about the **past**: something that already happened. The pattern is always the same:
**must / might / may / could / can't / couldn't + have + the third form**
The **third form** (bentuk ketiga, also called V3 or past participle) is the form you know from the present perfect: *gone, seen, eaten, left, forgotten*.
- *He **must have gone** home.* = Dia **pasti sudah** pulang.
- *She **might have overslept**.* = Dia **mungkin** kesiangan.
- *They **can't have seen** us.* = Mereka **tidak mungkin** melihat kita (tadi).

id.text:
**Ulasan singkat:** tentang **sekarang**, kamu sudah bisa bilang *He **must be** at home* (pasti), *He **might be** at home* (mungkin) dan *He **can't be** at home* (tidak mungkin).

Hari ini dugaannya tentang **masa lalu**: sesuatu yang sudah terjadi. Polanya selalu sama:
**must / might / may / could / can't / couldn't + have + bentuk ketiga**
**Bentuk ketiga** (V3, atau past participle) adalah bentuk yang kamu kenal dari present perfect: *gone, seen, eaten, left, forgotten*.
- *He **must have gone** home.* = Dia **pasti sudah** pulang.
- *She **might have overslept**.* = Dia **mungkin** kesiangan.
- *They **can't have seen** us.* = Mereka **tidak mungkin** melihat kita (tadi).

blocks.text:
**The Indonesian trap: where does the past go?** Indonesian has no tense, so *Dia pasti sudah pulang* tempts you to say 'He must went home'. But after **must, might, can't** the verb never changes into the past form. The past is shown by **have + the third form**: **He must have gone home.**
Three more traps:
- **have never changes**: not 'She can't has seen it', not 'had seen' → **She can't have seen it.**
- the **third** form, not the past form: not 'must have went' → **must have gone**.
- don't drop **be**: not 'You must have tired' → **You must have been tired.**

id.text:
**Jebakan bahasa Indonesia: di mana masa lalunya?** Bahasa Indonesia tidak punya tense, jadi *Dia pasti sudah pulang* membuatmu tergoda bilang 'He must went home'. Tapi sesudah **must, might, can't** kata kerjanya tidak pernah berubah ke bentuk lampau. Masa lalu ditunjukkan dengan **have + bentuk ketiga**: **He must have gone home.**
Tiga jebakan lain:
- **have tidak pernah berubah**: bukan 'She can't has seen it', bukan 'had seen' → **She can't have seen it.**
- bentuk **ketiga**, bukan bentuk lampau: bukan 'must have went' → **must have gone**.
- jangan hilangkan **be**: bukan 'You must have tired' → **You must have been tired.**

blocks.text:
**must have ≠ had to.** You know *had to* from B1: *He had to go home* = dia **harus** pulang (an obligation: someone or something made him go). *He must have gone home* = dia **pasti sudah** pulang (a guess from evidence).
**Spoken English:** *must have* usually sounds like **must've** ('mas-tev'), and *might have* like **might've**. Some native speakers even write 'must of', but that's a spelling mistake: write **must have** or **must've**.

id.text:
**must have ≠ had to.** Kamu sudah kenal *had to* dari B1: *He had to go home* = dia **harus** pulang (kewajiban: ada orang atau hal yang membuatnya pulang). *He must have gone home* = dia **pasti sudah** pulang (dugaan dari bukti).
**Bahasa lisan:** *must have* biasanya terdengar seperti **must've** ('mas-tev'), dan *might have* seperti **might've**. Sebagian penutur asli bahkan menulis 'must of', tapi itu salah eja: tulis **must have** atau **must've**.

blocks.prompt: There's a new box of cookies on the office table with a note: 'Happy Friday!'. The handwriting looks like Bu Ani's. Choose the correct sentence.
blocks.explain: Guess about the past = must + have + the third form: must have brought. 'must have bring' has no third form, and 'must brought' has no have.

id.title: must have, might have, can't have + bentuk ketiga

material.title: How sure are you about the past?

blocks.text:
It's the same scale you know from the present, with **have + the third form**. Here it is, from most sure *yes* to most sure *no*:
- **did** (past simple) = a fact, 100% yes
- **must have done** = almost sure: yes (*pasti sudah*)
- **might / may / could have done** = not sure (*mungkin*)
- **might not / may not have done** = not sure, maybe not (*mungkin tidak / mungkin belum*)
- **can't / couldn't have done** = almost sure: no (*tidak mungkin*)
- **didn't do** = a fact, 100% no
If you **know** what happened, don't guess: use the past simple.

id.text:
Skalanya sama dengan yang kamu kenal untuk masa sekarang, ditambah **have + bentuk ketiga**. Ini dia, dari paling yakin *ya* sampai paling yakin *tidak*:
- **did** (past simple) = fakta, 100% ya
- **must have done** = hampir pasti ya (*pasti sudah*)
- **might / may / could have done** = tidak yakin (*mungkin*)
- **might not / may not have done** = tidak yakin, mungkin tidak (*mungkin tidak / mungkin belum*)
- **can't / couldn't have done** = hampir pasti tidak (*tidak mungkin*)
- **didn't do** = fakta, 100% tidak
Kalau kamu **tahu** apa yang terjadi, jangan menduga: pakai past simple.

blocks.text:
**Not mustn't have: can't have.** Just like in the present, *mustn't* = **dilarang**, so 'He mustn't have known' is wrong for a guess. Say **He can't have known** (or *couldn't have known*, same meaning). In American films you may hear *He must not have known*: it's American English, but **can't have** is understood everywhere and is the safe choice.
**mungkin tidak ≠ tidak mungkin**, as before: *mungkin tidak / mungkin belum* = **might not have**, *tidak mungkin* = **can't have**.

id.text:
**Bukan mustn't have: can't have.** Sama seperti untuk masa sekarang, *mustn't* = **dilarang**, jadi 'He mustn't have known' salah untuk dugaan. Katakan **He can't have known** (atau *couldn't have known*, artinya sama). Di film Amerika kamu mungkin mendengar *He must not have known*: itu bahasa Inggris Amerika, tapi **can't have** dipahami di mana saja dan paling aman.
**mungkin tidak ≠ tidak mungkin**, seperti sebelumnya: *mungkin tidak / mungkin belum* = **might not have**, *tidak mungkin* = **can't have**.

blocks.explain: might have = mungkin: not sure. must have (almost sure yes) and can't have (almost sure no) both show the speaker is quite sure.

id.title: Seberapa yakin kamu tentang masa lalu?

material.title: From evidence now to what happened before

blocks.text:
A past guess usually starts with **evidence you see now**, and goes back to its **cause** (penyebab) earlier. *The floor is wet* (now) → *it must have rained* (before).
**How do you choose?** Look at the evidence:
- lots of clues, or only **one sensible explanation** → **must have**
- **one small clue**, or **many possible reasons** → **might / may / could have**
- the evidence makes it **impossible** → **can't / couldn't have**
Careful with time: *He **must be** tired* is about now; *He **must have been** tired* is about then.

id.text:
Dugaan tentang masa lalu biasanya dimulai dari **bukti yang kamu lihat sekarang**, lalu kembali ke **penyebab**nya sebelumnya. *The floor is wet* (sekarang) → *it must have rained* (sebelumnya).
**Bagaimana memilihnya?** Lihat buktinya:
- banyak petunjuk, atau hanya **satu penjelasan yang masuk akal** → **must have**
- **satu petunjuk kecil**, atau **banyak kemungkinan alasan** → **might / may / could have**
- buktinya membuat hal itu **mustahil** → **can't / couldn't have**
Hati-hati dengan waktu: *He **must be** tired* tentang sekarang; *He **must have been** tired* tentang waktu itu.

rows.en: The floor is wet. It must have rained.
Pak Hasan is very tanned after the long weekend. He must have been to the beach.
rows.id: Pak Hasan kulitnya jadi sangat gelap sesudah libur panjang. Dia pasti habis ke pantai.

rows.en: Sari's eyes are red. She might have been crying, or it might be an allergy.
rows.id: Mata Sari merah. Dia mungkin habis menangis, atau mungkin karena alergi.

rows.en: Dimas can't have cooked this. He doesn't know how to cook.
rows.id: Dimas tidak mungkin memasak ini. Dia tidak bisa masak.

blocks.text:
**must have been + -ing** = *pasti sedang …* at that time: *I called you at 11 and you didn't answer. You **must have been sleeping**.* (Kamu pasti sedang tidur waktu itu.) It works with might and can't too.
**could have has a second job.** In a guess, *could have* = *might have* (*He could have taken a taxi*). But *You could have called me!* = *kamu kan bisa menelepon aku!* (a complaint: you didn't call). For guesses, **might have** is the safest choice.

id.text:
**must have been + -ing** = *pasti sedang …* pada waktu itu: *I called you at 11 and you didn't answer. You **must have been sleeping**.* (Kamu pasti sedang tidur waktu itu.) Pola ini juga bisa dengan might dan can't.
**could have punya tugas kedua.** Dalam dugaan, *could have* = *might have* (*He could have taken a taxi*). Tapi *You could have called me!* = *kamu kan bisa menelepon aku!* (keluhan: kamu tidak menelepon). Untuk dugaan, **might have** paling aman.

blocks.prompt: This morning the road outside the kos is covered in fallen branches and leaves. Complete: There ___ a strong wind last night.
blocks.explain: The branches (evidence now) point back to last night: must have been. can't have been says the opposite of the evidence, and must be is about now, not last night.

id.prompt: Pagi ini jalan di depan kos penuh ranting dan daun yang jatuh. Lengkapi: There ___ a strong wind last night.
id.explain: Ranting-ranting itu (bukti sekarang) menunjuk ke tadi malam: must have been. can't have been berlawanan dengan buktinya, dan must be tentang sekarang, bukan tadi malam.

id.title: Dari bukti sekarang ke apa yang terjadi sebelumnya

material.title: needn't have vs didn't need to

blocks.text:
Both forms say something **wasn't necessary** in the past. The difference is one question: **did it happen?**
- **needn't have + the third form** = you **did** it, and later you found out it wasn't necessary → *ternyata tidak perlu (padahal sudah)*.
*I **needn't have brought** an umbrella. It didn't rain all day.* (I brought it, for nothing.)
- **didn't need to + base verb** = it wasn't necessary, **so usually you didn't do it** → *tidak perlu (jadi tidak)*.
*I **didn't need to bring** an umbrella. The event was indoors.* (I didn't bring one.)
You know *didn't have to* from B1: **didn't need to** means the same.

id.text:
Kedua bentuk ini bilang sesuatu **tidak perlu** di masa lalu. Bedanya ada di satu pertanyaan: **apakah itu terjadi?**
- **needn't have + bentuk ketiga** = kamu **sudah** melakukannya, lalu ternyata tidak perlu → *ternyata tidak perlu (padahal sudah)*.
*I **needn't have brought** an umbrella. It didn't rain all day.* (Aku sudah bawa, sia-sia.)
- **didn't need to + kata kerja dasar** = tidak perlu, **jadi biasanya kamu tidak melakukannya** → *tidak perlu (jadi tidak)*.
*I **didn't need to bring** an umbrella. The event was indoors.* (Aku tidak bawa.)
Kamu sudah kenal *didn't have to* dari B1: **didn't need to** artinya sama.

rows.en: I needn't have brought an umbrella. It didn't rain all day.
rows.id: Ternyata aku tidak perlu bawa payung (padahal sudah bawa). Seharian tidak hujan.

rows.en: We needn't have hurried. The train was 30 minutes late.
rows.id: Ternyata kita tidak perlu buru-buru (padahal sudah). Keretanya terlambat 30 menit.

rows.en: I didn't need to bring an umbrella. The event was indoors.
rows.id: Aku tidak perlu bawa payung (jadi tidak bawa). Acaranya di dalam ruangan.
rows.note: didn't bring it → didn't need to

rows.en: Budi didn't need to queue. He had booked his ticket online.
rows.id: Budi tidak perlu antre (jadi tidak antre). Dia sudah pesan tiket online.

blocks.text:
**Form traps:** needn't have + the **third** form: **needn't have brought**, not 'needn't have bring'. didn't need to + the **base** verb: **didn't need to bring**, not 'didn't need to brought'. And no *to* after needn't: not 'needn't to have'.
**Honest note:** *didn't need to* doesn't always mean you didn't do it: people sometimes say *I didn't need to bring it, but I did.* So *didn't need to* only says 'not necessary'; **needn't have** clearly says 'you did it'. In this lesson, the story always tells you whether it happened.
**British vs American:** *needn't have* is more British and a bit formal. Americans more often say *I didn't need to bring an umbrella after all* or *I didn't have to …*.

id.text:
**Jebakan bentuk:** needn't have + bentuk **ketiga**: **needn't have brought**, bukan 'needn't have bring'. didn't need to + kata kerja **dasar**: **didn't need to bring**, bukan 'didn't need to brought'. Dan tanpa *to* sesudah needn't: bukan 'needn't to have'.
**Catatan jujur:** *didn't need to* tidak selalu berarti kamu tidak melakukannya: orang kadang bilang *I didn't need to bring it, but I did.* Jadi *didn't need to* hanya bilang 'tidak perlu'; **needn't have** jelas bilang 'kamu sudah melakukannya'. Di pelajaran ini, ceritanya selalu memberi tahu apakah hal itu terjadi.
**Inggris vs Amerika:** *needn't have* lebih British dan agak formal. Orang Amerika lebih sering bilang *I didn't need to bring an umbrella after all* atau *I didn't have to …*.

blocks.text:
**needn't have ≠ shouldn't have.** Indonesian *seharusnya tidak perlu …* can push you to *shouldn't have*, but they're different:
- **needn't have** = it wasn't necessary: not wrong, just wasted time, money or effort. *We needn't have booked such a big room. Only five people came.*
- **shouldn't have** = *seharusnya tidak*: it was a mistake or a bad idea. *I shouldn't have eaten so much* (now I feel sick).
You'll practise should have / shouldn't have in the lesson on wishes and regrets.

id.text:
**needn't have ≠ shouldn't have.** Ungkapan *seharusnya tidak perlu …* bisa membuatmu tergoda memakai *shouldn't have*, padahal artinya berbeda:
- **needn't have** = ternyata tidak perlu: tidak salah, hanya buang waktu, uang atau tenaga. *We needn't have booked such a big room. Only five people came.*
- **shouldn't have** = *seharusnya tidak*: itu kesalahan atau ide yang buruk. *I shouldn't have eaten so much* (sekarang aku mual).
Kamu akan berlatih should have / shouldn't have di pelajaran tentang harapan dan penyesalan.

blocks.prompt: Budi printed 50 copies of the report for the meeting, but everyone read it on their laptops. Which sentence tells us that he DID print them, but it wasn't necessary?
options: He didn't need to print them.
blocks.explain: He printed them, and it turned out unnecessary → needn't have + the third form: needn't have printed. 'didn't need to print' only says it wasn't necessary (usually he didn't do it), and 'needn't have print' has no third form.

id.prompt: Budi mencetak 50 salinan laporan untuk rapat, tapi semua orang membacanya di laptop. Kalimat mana yang memberi tahu bahwa dia SUDAH mencetaknya, tapi ternyata tidak perlu?
id.explain: Dia sudah mencetaknya, dan ternyata tidak perlu → needn't have + bentuk ketiga: needn't have printed. 'didn't need to print' hanya bilang tidak perlu (biasanya dia tidak melakukannya), dan 'needn't have print' tidak memakai bentuk ketiga.

id.title: needn't have vs didn't need to

suggestedQuestions: Why can't I say 'He must went home'?
What's the difference between 'needn't have gone' and 'didn't need to go'?
Is 'might have' the same as 'could have'?
Why is it 'can't have' and not 'mustn't have'?

flashcards.back: must have + third form (He must have gone home.)
might / may / could have + third form (She might have overslept.)
can't / couldn't have + third form (They can't have seen us.)
might not / may not have + third form
needn't have + third form (I needn't have brought an umbrella.)
didn't need to + base verb (I didn't need to bring an umbrella.)

flashcards.front: Correct it: He must went home already.
flashcards.back: He must have gone home already.

flashcards.front: Correct it: I needn't have bring an umbrella.
flashcards.back: I needn't have brought an umbrella.

id.intro: Selamat datang lagi, detektif! Kamu sudah bisa menduga tentang sekarang dengan must be, might be dan can't be. Hari ini kita mundur ke masa lalu: lantainya basah, jadi pasti tadi hujan (it must have rained). Kamu juga akan belajar pasangan yang halus bedanya, needn't have dan didn't need to, untuk hal-hal yang ternyata tidak perlu.
suggestedQuestions: Kenapa saya tidak boleh bilang 'He must went home'?
Apa bedanya 'needn't have gone' dan 'didn't need to go'?

assessment.pmd-1: Perbaiki kesalahannya: Budi can't has finished the report already. He only started it ten minutes ago.
assessment.pmd-2: Sebelum rapat, kamu meninggalkan segelas penuh es kopi di mejamu. Sekarang gelasnya kosong, dan ada sedotan yang bukan punyamu di dalamnya. Lengkapi dengan bentuk yang benar dari drink: Somebody must ___ my coffee.
assessment.pmd-3: Budi gagal ujian SIM tiga kali. Kemarin dia dengan bangga menunjukkan SIM barunya (driving licence). Lengkapi dengan must have, might have atau can't have dan kata kerja pass: He ___ the test this time.
assessment.pmd-4: Rina bilang dia melihat Pak Hasan di kantor Bandung kemarin sore. Tapi kamu bersama Pak Hasan di sebuah konferensi di Surabaya seharian kemarin. Lengkapi dengan must have, might have atau can't have: He ___ been in Bandung yesterday afternoon.
assessment.pmd-5: Sari terlambat 20 menit untuk rapat pagi. Dia tidak mengangkat telepon, dan kamu sama sekali tidak tahu kenapa: banyak kemungkinan alasannya. Tulis satu dugaan dalam bahasa Inggris dengan might have, memakai: she / miss / the bus.
assessment.pmd-6: Kamu memasak rendang sepanci besar untuk tamu-tamumu. Waktu mereka datang, mereka bilang sudah makan di restoran. Lengkapi dengan cook supaya kalimatnya menunjukkan kamu SUDAH memasak, tapi ternyata tidak perlu: I ___ so much food.
assessment.pmd-7: Rina berencana memesan Grab ke Stasiun Gambir. Lalu kakaknya menawarkan untuk mengantarnya, jadi dia tidak memesan. Lengkapi dengan needn't have atau didn't need to dan kata kerja book: She ___ a Grab.
